admission.justification: Two other designs for what finalization does to a master were weighed and rejected, and every later change to finalization or to the retire operation has to keep a master's folder in place until it is retired explicitly.

alternatives.option: Finalizing a master never archives it, with or without a sprint. The explicit retire operation is the only route that archives a master, and when a sprint commands the master it removes the master from the sprint in the same step.
alternatives.reason: The developer ruled that there is no point archiving individual masters that belong to a sprint, and that getting rid of or abandoning a master is a different intent that must also remove it from the sprint. Finalization states a master is done; it is not a request to get rid of it, and the archive hook it would run deletes artifacts irreversibly.

alternatives.option: Archive a master when it is finalized.
alternatives.reason: It moves the folder a sprint still names and breaks the sprint's topology for every tool that reads it; it also runs the deleting archive hook for a master nobody asked to get rid of.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A sprint no longer requires each commanded master to resolve to a live folder, and the archive hook's deletions can be undone.

alternatives.option: At finalization, archive only the masters that no sprint commands.
alternatives.reason: It was the premise of the earlier packet versions, but on the landed code finalization never archived such a master, and no ruling asked for it; it would also delete artifacts at finalization without a request to get rid of the master.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The developer asks for finalization of a standalone master to archive it.

consequences: A finalized master a sprint commands stays in place, its sprint row reads Completed, and the result names the sprint as the reason the archive was skipped.
A finalized master no sprint commands stays in place, and the result names task_doc.retire_master as the only archive route.
Retiring a master works with and without a sprint and is the only route that archives one.
context: The architect tried to archive the completed masters ICR and KS after finalization. Archiving a sprint's master moved a folder that the sprint still named, which made the sprint invalid, and the operations that could repair a sprint refused while the master was gone. Version 2 of the requirement assumed that a master that no sprint commands was archived at finalization as before; on the landed code that never happened, because a task folder that holds a series-contract.md is skipped by the archive step.
decider: developer (260928-MIK DEVELOPER-DIRECTION D41, confirmed by D47) and the architect's ruling 2 of run 2 for the case of a master that no sprint commands

evidence: DEVELOPER-DIRECTION D41 (2026-10-02) and D47 (2026-10-04); notes/ARCHITECT-RUN-2.md ruling 2 of run 2; requirements/MIK-R41-v3-abandoned-leaves-do-not-block-a-master.md rule 3
